# sys

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** API Collection

Access general system utilities for time, file systems, and system information.

## Topics

### Block Device

- [bdevsw_add](1457957-bdevsw_add.md)
- [bdevsw_isfree](1457925-bdevsw_isfree.md)
- [bdevsw_remove](1457943-bdevsw_remove.md)
- [cdevsw_add](1457951-cdevsw_add.md)
- [cdevsw_add_with_bdev](1458015-cdevsw_add_with_bdev.md)
- [cdevsw_isfree](1457965-cdevsw_isfree.md)
- [cdevsw_remove](1458013-cdevsw_remove.md)

### Buffers

- [buf_alloc](1561906-buf_alloc.md): Allocate an uninitialized buffer.
- [buf_attr](1561894-buf_attr.md): Gets the attributes for this buf.
- [buf_bawrite](1561823-buf_bawrite.md): Start an asychronous write on a buffer.
- [buf_bdwrite](1561858-buf_bdwrite.md): Mark a buffer for delayed write.
- [buf_biodone](1561914-buf_biodone.md): Mark an I/O as completed.
- [buf_biowait](1561908-buf_biowait.md): Wait for I/O on a buffer to complete.
- [buf_blkno](1561926-buf_blkno.md): Get physical block number associated with a buffer, in the sense of VNOP_BLOCKMAP.
- [buf_bread](1561851-buf_bread.md): Synchronously read a block of a file.
- [buf_breadn](1561873-buf_breadn.md): Read a block from a file with read-ahead.
- [buf_brelse](1561897-buf_brelse.md): Release any claim to a buffer, sending it back to free lists.
- [buf_bwrite](1561886-buf_bwrite.md): Write a buffer's data to backing store.
- [buf_callback](1561902-buf_callback.md): Get the function set to be called when I/O on a buffer completes.
- [buf_clear](1561901-buf_clear.md): Zero out the storage associated with a buffer.
- [buf_clear_redundancy_flags](1561898-buf_clear_redundancy_flags.md): Clear flags on a buffer. @discussion: buffer_redundancy_flags &= ~flags
- [buf_clearflags](1561837-buf_clearflags.md): Clear flags on a buffer. @discussion: buffer_flags &= ~flags
- [buf_clone](1561867-buf_clone.md): Clone a buffer with a restricted range and an optional callback.
- [buf_count](1561820-buf_count.md): Get count of valid bytes in a buffer. This may be less than the space allocated to the buffer.
- [buf_create_shadow](1561838-buf_create_shadow.md): Create a shadow buffer with optional private storage and an optional callback.
- [buf_dataptr](1561881-buf_dataptr.md): Get the address at which a buffer's data is stored; for iobufs, this must be set with buf_setdataptr(). See buf_map().
- [buf_device](1561922-buf_device.md): Get the device ID associated with a buffer.
- [buf_dirtyend](1561850-buf_dirtyend.md): Get the ending offset of the dirty region associated with a buffer.
- [buf_dirtyoff](1561923-buf_dirtyoff.md): Get the starting offset of the dirty region associated with a buffer.
- [buf_drvdata](1561866-buf_drvdata.md): Get driver-specific data from a buffer.
- [buf_error](1561818-buf_error.md): Get the error value associated with a buffer.
- [buf_flags](1561844-buf_flags.md): Get flags set on a buffer.
- [buf_flushdirtyblks](1561822-buf_flushdirtyblks.md): Write dirty file blocks to disk.
- [buf_free](1561907-buf_free.md): Free a buffer that was allocated with buf_alloc().
- [buf_fromcache](1561933-buf_fromcache.md): Check if a buffer's data was found in core.
- [buf_fsprivate](1561929-buf_fsprivate.md): Get filesystem-specific data from a buffer.
- [buf_fua](1561842-buf_fua.md): Check if a buffer is marked for write through disk caches.
- [buf_getblk](1561932-buf_getblk.md): Traditional buffer cache routine to get a buffer corresponding to a logical block in a file.
- [buf_geteblk](1561862-buf_geteblk.md): Get a metadata buffer which is marked invalid and not associated with any vnode.
- [buf_invalblkno](1561843-buf_invalblkno.md): Invalidate a filesystem logical block in a file.
- [buf_invalidateblks](1561910-buf_invalidateblks.md): Invalidate all the blocks associated with a vnode.
- [buf_iterate](1561857-buf_iterate.md): Perform some operation on all buffers associated with a vnode.
- [buf_lblkno](1561825-buf_lblkno.md): Get logical block number associated with a buffer.
- [buf_map](1561890-buf_map.md): Get virtual mappings for buffer data.
- [buf_markaged](1561845-buf_markaged.md): Mark a buffer as "aged," i.e. as a good candidate to be discarded and reused after buf_brelse().
- [buf_markclean](1561834-buf_markclean.md)
- [buf_markdelayed](1561911-buf_markdelayed.md): Mark a buffer as a delayed write: mark it dirty without actually scheduling I/O.
- [buf_markeintr](1561892-buf_markeintr.md): Mark a buffer as having been interrupted during I/O.
- [buf_markfua](1561841-buf_markfua.md): Mark a buffer for write through disk cache, if disk supports it.
- [buf_markinvalid](1561863-buf_markinvalid.md): Mark a buffer as not having valid data and being ready for immediate reuse after buf_brelse().
- [buf_markstatic](1561839-buf_markstatic.md): Mark a buffer as being likely to contain static data.

# Document: thread_call_priority_t

Source path: documentation/kernel/thread_call_priority_t
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/thread_call_priority_t
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# thread_call_priority_t

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Enumeration  
**Availability:** macOS 10.8+

## Declaration

```objectivec
typedef enum thread_call_priority_t : unsigned int {
    ...
} thread_call_priority_t;
```

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Thread call priorities should not be assumed to have any specific numerical value; they should be interpreted as importances or roles for work items, priorities for which will be reasonably managed by the subsystem.

## Topics

### Constants

- [THREAD_CALL_PRIORITY_HIGH](thread_call_priority_t/thread_call_priority_high.md)
- [THREAD_CALL_PRIORITY_KERNEL](thread_call_priority_t/thread_call_priority_kernel.md)
- [THREAD_CALL_PRIORITY_USER](thread_call_priority_t/thread_call_priority_user.md)
- [THREAD_CALL_PRIORITY_LOW](thread_call_priority_t/thread_call_priority_low.md)
- [THREAD_CALL_PRIORITY_KERNEL_HIGH](thread_call_priority_t/thread_call_priority_kernel_high.md)

# Document: THREAD_CALL_PRIORITY_HIGH

Source path: documentation/kernel/thread_call_priority_t/thread_call_priority_high
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/thread_call_priority_t/thread_call_priority_high
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# THREAD_CALL_PRIORITY_HIGH

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Enumeration Case  
**Availability:** macOS 10.8+

## Declaration

```objectivec
THREAD_CALL_PRIORITY_HIGH = 0
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Importance above everything but realtime. Thread calls allocated with this priority execute at extremely high priority, above everything but realtime threads. They are generally executed in serial. Though they may execute concurrently under some circumstances, no fan-out is implied. These work items should do very small amounts of work or risk disrupting system responsiveness.

# Document: tIOUSBDescriptorType

Source path: documentation/kernel/tiousbdescriptortype
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/tiousbdescriptortype
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# tIOUSBDescriptorType

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Type Alias  
**Availability:** macOS 10.15+

Constants describing the types of descriptors available for a USB device.

## Declaration

```objectivec
typedef enum tIOUSBDescriptorType tIOUSBDescriptorType;
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

When you fetch descriptors from a USB device, the data includes a one-byte value that indicates the type of the descriptor. Use these constants to determine the type. 

For detailed information about the descriptor types, see USB 3.2, 9.4.

## Topics

### Getting the Descriptor Type

- [kIOUSBDecriptorTypeHID](tiousbdescriptortype/kiousbdecriptortypehid.md): The type for a human interaction device descriptor.

- [kIOUSBDescriptorTypePhysical](tiousbdescriptortype/kiousbdescriptortypephysical.md): The type for a physical descriptor.

## Topics

### Instance Properties

- [isub_image](twolevel_hint/1525623-isub_image.md): The subimage in which the symbol is defined. It is an index into the list of images that make up the umbrella image. If this field is 0, the symbol is in the umbrella image itself. If the image is not an umbrella framework or library, this field is 0.
- [itoc](twolevel_hint/1525807-itoc.md): The symbol index into the table of contents of the image specified by the `isub_image` field.

# Document: USBDeviceInformationBits

Source path: documentation/kernel/usbdeviceinformationbits
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/usbdeviceinformationbits
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# USBDeviceInformationBits

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Type Alias  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

The state of a USB device.

## Declaration

```objectivec
typedef enum USBDeviceInformationBits USBDeviceInformationBits;
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

[GetUSBDeviceInformation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/iousbdeviceinterface942/2977165-getusbdeviceinformation) returns a `unit32_t` value with bits set indicating that a particular state is present in the USB device.

## Topics

### Constants

- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsCaptiveBit](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceiscaptivebit.md): The USB device has directly attached to its hub and isn’t removable.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsAttachedToRootHubBit](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisattachedtoroothubbit.md): The USB device has directly attached to the root hub.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsInternalBit](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisinternalbit.md): The USB device is internal to the enclosure.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsConnectedBit](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisconnectedbit.md): The system has connected the USB device to its hub.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsEnabledBit](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisenabledbit.md): The system has enabled the hub port that the USB device attaches to.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsSuspendedBit](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceissuspendedbit.md): The system has suspended the hub port that the USB device attaches to.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsInResetBit](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisinresetbit.md): The system is resetting the hub port that the USB attaches to.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceOvercurrentBit](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceovercurrentbit.md): The USB device generated an overcurrent.
- [kUSBInformationDevicePortIsInTestModeBit](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceportisintestmodebit.md): The hub port that the USB device attaches to is in test mode.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsRootHub](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisroothub.md): The device is the root hub simulation.
- [kUSBInformationRootHubisBuiltIn](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationroothubisbuiltin.md): The USB root hub is built-in.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsRemote](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisremote.md): This device attaches to the controller through a remote connection.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsAttachedToEnclosure](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisattachedtoenclosure.md): The hub port that the USB device connects to has a USB connector on the enclosure.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsOnThunderbolt](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisonthunderbolt): The USB device is downstream of a controller that attaches through a Thunderbolt port.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsAttachedToEnclosureMask](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisattachedtoenclosuremask.md): The mask indicating that the USB device has attached to an enclosure.
- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsAttachedToRootHubMask](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisattachedtoroothubmask.md): The mask indicating that the USB device has attached to a root hub.

- [kUSBInformationDeviceIsOnThunderboltBit](usbdeviceinformationbits/kusbinformationdeviceisonthunderboltbit.md): The bit indicating that the USB device is on a Thunderbolt port.

```objectivec
kUSBInformationRootHubisBuiltIn = 10
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If this is a root hub simulation and it’s built in to the enclosure, this bit is set. If it’s on an expansion card, this bit is clear.

# Document: USBNotificationTypes

Source path: documentation/kernel/usbnotificationtypes
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/usbnotificationtypes
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# USBNotificationTypes

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Type Alias  
**Availability:** macOS 10.9+

Defines types of USB notifications.

## Declaration

```objectivec
typedef enum USBNotificationTypes USBNotificationTypes;
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Use this enumeration to register for USB notifications. You can OR these types together if you need more than one notification. Acknowledge each notification before the process (system sleep or system wake) continues. See [RegisterForNotification](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/iousbinterfaceinterface942/2977241-registerfornotification) and [AcknowledgeNotification](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/iousbdeviceinterface942/2977134-acknowledgenotification) for more information.

## Topics

### Constants

- [kUSBNotificationPreForcedSuspend](usbnotificationtypes/kusbnotificationpreforcedsuspend.md): The system sends a notification prior to a forced suspend.
- [kUSBNotificationPostForcedSuspend](usbnotificationtypes/kusbnotificationpostforcedsuspend.md): The system sends a notification after a forced suspend completes.
- [kUSBNotificationPreForcedResume](usbnotificationtypes/kusbnotificationpreforcedresume.md): The system sends a notification before a resume, which occurs after a forced suspend.
- [kUSBNotificationPostForcedResume](usbnotificationtypes/kusbnotificationpostforcedresume.md): The system sends a notification after a resume, which occurs after a forced suspend.

# kUSBPowerDuringWakeRevocable

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Enumeration Case  
**Availability:** macOS 10.8+

The system requests power reallocation as revocable.

## Declaration

```objectivec
kUSBPowerDuringWakeRevocable = 6
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The system uses this extra power while it’s awake, but the [kUSBPowerRequestWakeRelease](kusbpowerrequestwakerelease.md) message can take that power away and reallocate it to another device.

# Document: kUSBPowerDuringWakeUSB3

# kUSBPowerDuringWakeUSB3

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Enumeration Case  
**Availability:** macOS 10.8+

The system requests extra power allocation.

## Declaration

```objectivec
kUSBPowerDuringWakeUSB3 = 7
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The USB stack uses this enumeration to allocate the 400 milliamps extra for USB 3.0 above the 500 milliamps that USB 2.0 allocates.

# Document: kUSBAddExtraResetTimeBit

Source path: documentation/kernel/usbreenumerateoptions/kusbaddextraresettimebit
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/usbreenumerateoptions/kusbaddextraresettimebit
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# kUSBAddExtraResetTimeBit

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Enumeration Case  
**Availability:** macOS 10.3+

Request extra time after reset.

## Declaration

```objectivec
kUSBAddExtraResetTimeBit = 31
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Setting this bit causes the hub driver to wait 100 milliseconds before addressing the device after the reset following the reenumeration.

# Document: kUSBAddExtraResetTimeMask

# kUSBAddExtraResetTimeMask

**Kind:** Enumeration Case  
**Availability:** macOS 10.3+

The mask to request extra time after reset.

## Declaration

```objectivec

```

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vfs

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** API Collection

Access the virtual file-system interfaces.

## Topics

### Functions

- [vflush](1562120-vflush.md): Reclaim the vnodes for a mount.
- [vfs_64bitready](1523312-vfs_64bitready.md): Check if the filesystem associated with a mountpoint is marked ready for interaction with 64-bit user processes.
- [vfs_addname](1562422-vfs_addname.md): Deprecated
- [vfs_attr_pack](1562242-vfs_attr_pack.md)
- [vfs_attr_pack_ext](3353091-vfs_attr_pack_ext.md)
- [vfs_authcache_ttl](1523180-vfs_authcache_ttl.md): Determine the time-to-live of cached authorized credentials for files in this filesystem.
- [vfs_authopaque](1523276-vfs_authopaque.md): Determine if a filesystem's authorization decisions occur remotely.
- [vfs_authopaqueaccess](1523247-vfs_authopaqueaccess.md): Check if a filesystem is marked as having reliable remote VNOP_ACCESS support.
- [vfs_busy](1523389-vfs_busy.md): "Busy" a mountpoint.
- [vfs_clearauthcache_ttl](1523469-vfs_clearauthcache_ttl.md): Remove time-to-live controls for cached credentials on a filesytem. Filesystems with remote authorization decisions (opaque) will still have KAUTH_VNODE_SEARCH rights cached for a default of CACHED_LOOKUP_RIGHT_TTL seconds.
- [vfs_clearauthopaque](1523223-vfs_clearauthopaque.md)
- [vfs_clearauthopaqueaccess](1523231-vfs_clearauthopaqueaccess.md): Mark a filesystem as not having remote VNOP_ACCESS support.
- [vfs_clearextendedsecurity](1523368-vfs_clearextendedsecurity.md): Mark a filesystem as NOT supporting security controls beyond POSIX permissions.
- [vfs_clearflags](1523299-vfs_clearflags.md): Clear flags on a mount.
- [vfs_context_create](1562360-vfs_context_create.md): Create a new vfs_context_t with appropriate references held.
- [vfs_context_current](1562223-vfs_context_current.md): Get the vfs_context for the current thread, or the kernel context if there is no context for current thread.
- [vfs_context_get_special_port](1562113-vfs_context_get_special_port.md)
- [vfs_context_is64bit](1562122-vfs_context_is64bit.md): Determine if a vfs_context_t corresponds to a 64-bit user process.
- [vfs_context_issignal](1562448-vfs_context_issignal.md): Get a bitfield of pending signals for the BSD process associated with a vfs_context_t.
- [vfs_context_pid](1562461-vfs_context_pid.md): Get the process id of the BSD process associated with a vfs_context_t.
- [vfs_context_proc](1562390-vfs_context_proc.md): Get the BSD process structure associated with a vfs_context_t.
- [vfs_context_rele](1562367-vfs_context_rele.md): Release references on components of a context and deallocate it.
- [vfs_context_set_special_port](1562263-vfs_context_set_special_port.md)
- [vfs_context_suser](1562261-vfs_context_suser.md): Determine if a vfs_context_t corresponds to the superuser.
- [vfs_context_ucred](1562308-vfs_context_ucred.md): Get the credential associated with a vfs_context_t.
- [vfs_devblocksize](1523172-vfs_devblocksize.md): Get the block size of the device underlying a mount.
- [vfs_event_init](1523461-vfs_event_init.md): This function should not be called by kexts.
- [vfs_event_signal](1523107-vfs_event_signal.md): Post a kqueue-style event on a filesystem (EVFILT_FS).
- [vfs_flags](1523261-vfs_flags.md): Retrieve mount flags.
- [vfs_fsadd](1523490-vfs_fsadd.md): Register a filesystem with VFS.
- [vfs_fsprivate](1523301-vfs_fsprivate.md): Get filesystem-private mount data.
- [vfs_fsremove](1523194-vfs_fsremove.md): Unregister a filesystem with VFS.
- [vfs_get_notify_attributes](1562277-vfs_get_notify_attributes.md)
- [vfs_getnewfsid](1523259-vfs_getnewfsid.md): Generate a unique filesystem ID for a mount and store it in the mount structure.
- [vfs_getvfs](1523465-vfs_getvfs.md): Given a filesystem ID, look up a mount structure.
- [vfs_init_io_attributes](1523109-vfs_init_io_attributes.md): Set I/O attributes on a mountpoint based on device properties.
- [vfs_ioattr](1523411-vfs_ioattr.md): Get I/O attributes associated with a mounpoint.
- [vfs_isforce](1523525-vfs_isforce.md): Determine if a forced unmount is in progress.
- [vfs_isrdonly](1523242-vfs_isrdonly.md): Determine if a filesystem is mounted read-only.
- [vfs_isrdwr](1523454-vfs_isrdwr.md): Determine if a filesystem is mounted with writes enabled.
- [vfs_isreload](1523537-vfs_isreload.md): Determine if a reload of filesystem data is in progress. This can only be the case for a read-only filesystem; all data is brought in from secondary storage.
- [vfs_issynchronous](1523327-vfs_issynchronous.md): Determine if writes to a filesystem occur synchronously.
- [vfs_isunmount](1523380-vfs_isunmount.md): Determine if an unmount is in progress.
- [vfs_isupdate](1523536-vfs_isupdate.md): Determine if a mount update is in progress.
- [vfs_iswriteupgrade](1523486-vfs_iswriteupgrade.md): Determine if a filesystem is mounted read-only but a request has been made to upgrade to read-write.
- [vfs_iterate](1523233-vfs_iterate.md): Iterate over all mountpoints with a callback. Used, for example, by sync().
- [vfs_maxsymlen](1523507-vfs_maxsymlen.md): Get the maximum length of a symbolic link on a filesystem.
- [vfs_mountedon](1523197-vfs_mountedon.md): Check whether a given block device has a filesystem mounted on it.
- [vfs_name](1523128-vfs_name.md): Copy filesystem name into a buffer.
- [vfs_nspace_server](3042879-vfs_nspace_server.md)
- [vfs_nspace_server_routine](3042880-vfs_nspace_server_routine.md)
- [vfs_removename](1562343-vfs_removename.md): Deprecated
- [vfs_rootvnode](1562439-vfs_rootvnode.md): Returns the root vnode with an iocount.
- [vfs_set_root_unmounted_cleanly](2872995-vfs_set_root_unmounted_cleanly.md)
- [vfs_setauthcache_ttl](1523286-vfs_setauthcache_ttl.md): Enable credential caching and set time-to-live of cached authorized credentials for files in this filesystem.
- [vfs_setauthopaque](1523440-vfs_setauthopaque.md): Mark a filesystem as having authorization decisions controlled remotely.
- [vfs_setauthopaqueaccess](1523218-vfs_setauthopaqueaccess.md): Mark a filesystem as having remote VNOP_ACCESS support.
- [vfs_setextendedsecurity](1523360-vfs_setextendedsecurity.md): Mark a filesystem as supporting security controls beyond POSIX permissions.
- [vfs_setflags](1523521-vfs_setflags.md): Set flags on a mount.
- [vfs_setfsprivate](1523413-vfs_setfsprivate.md): Set filesystem-private mount data.
- [vfs_setioattr](1523458-vfs_setioattr.md): Set I/O attributes associated with a mounpoint.
- [vfs_setlocklocal](1523104-vfs_setlocklocal.md): Mark a filesystem as using VFS-level advisory locking support.
- [vfs_setmaxsymlen](1523316-vfs_setmaxsymlen.md): Set the maximum length of a symbolic link on a filesystem.
- [vfs_setup_vattr_from_attrlist](1562135-vfs_setup_vattr_from_attrlist.md)
- [vfs_statfs](1523098-vfs_statfs.md): Get information about filesystem status.
- [vfs_typenum](1523418-vfs_typenum.md): Get (archaic) filesystem type number.
- [vfs_unbusy](1523451-vfs_unbusy.md): "Unbusy" a mountpoint by releasing its read-write lock.
- [vfs_unmountbyfsid](1523503-vfs_unmountbyfsid.md): Find a filesystem by ID and unmount it.
- [vfs_update_vfsstat](1523278-vfs_update_vfsstat.md): Update cached filesystem status information in the VFS mount structure.

### BSD

- [architecture](architecture.md): Access machine-level and architectural information about the current platform.

- [vnop_mkdir_args](vnop_mkdir_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to rename a file.
- [vnop_mknod_args](vnop_mknod_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to create a whiteout.
- [vnop_mmap_args](vnop_mmap_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to invalidate all open file descriptors for a vnode.
- [vnop_mmap_check_args](vnop_mmap_check_args.md)
- [vnop_mnomap_args](vnop_mnomap_args.md): Notify a filesystem that a file is being mmap-ed.
- [vnop_offtoblk_args](vnop_offtoblk_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to convert a logical block number to a file offset.
- [vnop_open_args](vnop_open_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to create a special file.
- [vnop_pagein_args](vnop_pagein_args.md): Pre-allocate space for a file.
- [vnop_pageout_args](vnop_pageout_args.md): Pull file data into memory.
- [vnop_pathconf_args](vnop_pathconf_args.md): Release filesystem-internal resources for a vnode.
- [vnop_read_args](vnop_read_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to set vnode attributes.
- [vnop_readdir_args](vnop_readdir_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to create a symbolic link.
- [vnop_readdirattr_args](vnop_readdirattr_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to enumerate directory entries.
- [vnop_readlink_args](vnop_readlink_args.md): Call down to get file attributes for many files in a directory at once.
- [vnop_reclaim_args](vnop_reclaim_args.md): Notify a filesystem that the last usecount (persistent reference) on a vnode has been dropped.
- [vnop_remove_args](vnop_remove_args.md)
- [vnop_removexattr_args](vnop_removexattr_args.md)
- [vnop_rename_args](vnop_rename_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to create a hardlink to a file.
- [vnop_renamex_args](vnop_renamex_args.md)
- [vnop_revoke_args](vnop_revoke_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to atomically exchange the data of two files.
- [vnop_rmdir_args](vnop_rmdir_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to create a directory.
- [vnop_searchfs_args](vnop_searchfs_args.md): Write data from a mapped file back to disk.
- [vnop_select_args](vnop_select_args.md)
- [vnop_setattr_args](vnop_setattr_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to get vnode attributes.
- [vnop_setlabel_args](vnop_setlabel_args.md)
- [vnop_setxattr_args](vnop_setxattr_args.md)
- [vnop_strategy_args](vnop_strategy_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to get information about the on-disk layout of a file region.
- [vnop_symlink_args](vnop_symlink_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to delete a directory.
- [vnop_whiteout_args](vnop_whiteout_args.md): Call down to a filesystem to create a regular file (VREG).
- [vnop_write_args](vnop_write_args.md)

# Document: vnop_access_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_access_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_access_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_access_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to close a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_access_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The close vnop gives a filesystem a chance to release state set up by a VNOP_OPEN(). VFS promises to send down exactly one VNOP_CLOSE() for each VNOP_OPEN().

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_access_args/1807054-vp.md): File to close.
- [fflag](vnop_access_args/1807056-fflag.md): FREAD and/or FWRITE; in the case of a file opened with open(2), fflag corresponds to how the file was opened.
- [ctx](vnop_access_args/1807060-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate close.

### Instance Properties

- [a_action](vnop_access_args/1586118-a_action.md)
- [a_context](vnop_access_args/1586233-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_access_args/1586046-a_desc.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_access_args/1585970-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_advlock_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_advlock_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_advlock_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_advlock_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Query a filesystem for path properties.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_advlock_args {
    ...
};
```

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_advlock_args/1807064-vp.md): The vnode whose filesystem to query.
- [name](vnop_advlock_args/1807068-name.md): Which property to request: see unistd.h. For example: \_PC_CASE_SENSITIVE (is a filesystem case-sensitive?). Only one property can be requested at a time.
- [retval](vnop_advlock_args/1807072-retval.md): Destination for value of property.
- [ctx](vnop_advlock_args/1807076-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pathconf request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_advlock_args/1586054-a_context.md)

# Document: vnop_allocate_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_allocate_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_allocate_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_allocate_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Aquire or release and advisory lock on a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_allocate_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Advisory locking is somewhat complicated. VNOP_ADVLOCK is overloaded for both flock() and POSIX advisory locking usage, though not all filesystems support both (or any). VFS provides an advisory locking mechanism for filesystems which can take advantage of it; vfs_setlocklocal() marks a filesystem as using VFS advisory locking support.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_allocate_args/1807080-vp.md): The vnode to lock or unlock.
- [id](vnop_allocate_args/1807083-id.md): Identifier for lock holder: ignored by most filesystems.
- [op](vnop_allocate_args/1807086-op.md): Which locking operation: F_SETLK: set locking information about a region. F_GETLK: get locking information about the specified region. F_UNLCK: Unlock a region.
- [fl](vnop_allocate_args/1807089-fl.md): Description of file region to lock. l_whence is as with "lseek." Includes a type: F_RDLCK (shared lock), F_UNLCK (unlock) , and F_WRLCK (exclusive lock).
- [flags](vnop_allocate_args/1807092-flags.md): F_FLOCK: use flock() semantics. F_POSIX: use POSIX semantics. F_WAIT: sleep if necessary. F_PROV: Non-coelesced provisional lock (unused in xnu).
- [ctx](vnop_allocate_args/1807096-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for advisory locking request.
- [timeout](vnop_allocate_args/1807102-timeout.md): Timespec for timeout in case of F_SETLKWTIMEOUT.

The vnode to lock or unlock.

## See Also

### Fields

- [id](1807083-id.md): Identifier for lock holder: ignored by most filesystems.
- [op](1807086-op.md): Which locking operation: F_SETLK: set locking information about a region. F_GETLK: get locking information about the specified region. F_UNLCK: Unlock a region.
- [fl](1807089-fl.md): Description of file region to lock. l_whence is as with "lseek." Includes a type: F_RDLCK (shared lock), F_UNLCK (unlock) , and F_WRLCK (exclusive lock).
- [flags](1807092-flags.md): F_FLOCK: use flock() semantics. F_POSIX: use POSIX semantics. F_WAIT: sleep if necessary. F_PROV: Non-coelesced provisional lock (unused in xnu).
- [ctx](1807096-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for advisory locking request.
- [timeout](1807102-timeout.md): Timespec for timeout in case of F_SETLKWTIMEOUT.

Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_allocate_args/1807083-id
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# id

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Identifier for lock holder: ignored by most filesystems.

## See Also

### Fields

- [vp](1807080-vp.md): The vnode to lock or unlock.
- [op](1807086-op.md): Which locking operation: F_SETLK: set locking information about a region. F_GETLK: get locking information about the specified region. F_UNLCK: Unlock a region.
- [fl](1807089-fl.md): Description of file region to lock. l_whence is as with "lseek." Includes a type: F_RDLCK (shared lock), F_UNLCK (unlock) , and F_WRLCK (exclusive lock).
- [flags](1807092-flags.md): F_FLOCK: use flock() semantics. F_POSIX: use POSIX semantics. F_WAIT: sleep if necessary. F_PROV: Non-coelesced provisional lock (unused in xnu).
- [ctx](1807096-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for advisory locking request.
- [timeout](1807102-timeout.md): Timespec for timeout in case of F_SETLKWTIMEOUT.

# Document: vnop_blktooff_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_blktooff_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_blktooff_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_blktooff_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

List extended attribute keys.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_blktooff_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Should write a sequence of unseparated, null-terminated extended-attribute names into the space described by the provided uio. These keys can then be passed to getxattr() (and VNOP_GETXATTR()).

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_blktooff_args/1807112-vp.md): The vnode for which to get extended attribute keys.
- [uio](vnop_blktooff_args/1807117-uio.md): Description of target memory for attribute keys.
- [size](vnop_blktooff_args/1807118-size.md): Should be set to amount of data written to buffer.
- [options](vnop_blktooff_args/1807120-options.md): XATTR_NOSECURITY: bypass security checking.
- [ctx](vnop_blktooff_args/1807122-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for attribute name request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_desc](vnop_blktooff_args/1585965-a_desc.md)
- [a_lblkno](vnop_blktooff_args/1585968-a_lblkno.md)
- [a_offset](vnop_blktooff_args/1586226-a_offset.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_blktooff_args/1586060-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_close_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_close_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_close_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_close_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to open a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_close_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The open vnop gives a filesystem a chance to initialize a file for operations like reading, writing, and ioctls. VFS promises to send down exactly one VNOP_CLOSE() for each VNOP_OPEN().

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_close_args/1807145-vp.md): File to open.
- [mode](vnop_close_args/1807149-mode.md): FREAD and/or FWRITE.
- [ctx](vnop_close_args/1807152-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate open.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_close_args/1586002-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_close_args/1586142-a_desc.md)
- [a_fflag](vnop_close_args/1586290-a_fflag.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_close_args/1586251-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_copyfile_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_copyfile_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_copyfile_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_copyfile_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Write data from a mapped file back to disk.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_copyfile_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_PAGEOUT() is called when data from a mapped file needs to be flushed to disk, either because of an msync() call or due to memory pressure. Filesystems are for the most part expected to just call cluster_pageout(). However, if they opt into the VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 flag, then they will be responsible for creating their own UPLs.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_copyfile_args/1807157-vp.md): The vnode for which to page out data.
- [pl](vnop_copyfile_args/1807159-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](vnop_copyfile_args/1807160-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](vnop_copyfile_args/1807161-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [size](vnop_copyfile_args/1807165-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [flags](vnop_copyfile_args/1807170-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](vnop_copyfile_args/1807178-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

# Document: vp

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_copyfile_args/1807157-vp
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_copyfile_args/1807157-vp
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vp

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The vnode for which to page out data.

## See Also

### Fields

- [pl](1807159-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](1807160-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](1807161-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [size](1807165-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [flags](1807170-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](1807178-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

# Document: vnop_create_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_create_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_create_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_create_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to look for a directory entry by name.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_create_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_LOOKUP is the key pathway through which VFS asks a filesystem to find a file. The vnode should be returned with an iocount to be dropped by the caller. A VNOP_LOOKUP() calldown can come without a preceding VNOP_OPEN().

## Topics

### Fields

- [dvp](vnop_create_args/1807191-dvp.md): Directory in which to look up file.
- [vpp](vnop_create_args/1807195-vpp.md): Destination for found vnode.
- [cnp](vnop_create_args/1807198-cnp.md): Structure describing filename to find, reason for lookup, and various other data.
- [ctx](vnop_create_args/1807203-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate lookup request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_cnp](vnop_create_args/1586179-a_cnp.md)
- [a_context](vnop_create_args/1586176-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_create_args/1586308-a_desc.md)
- [a_dvp](vnop_create_args/1586267-a_dvp.md)
- [a_vap](vnop_create_args/1586280-a_vap.md)
- [a_vpp](vnop_create_args/1586171-a_vpp.md)

# Document: vnop_exchange_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_exchange_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_exchange_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_exchange_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem or device to check if a file is ready for I/O and request later notification if it is not currently ready.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_exchange_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

In general, regular are always "ready for I/O" and their select vnops simply return "1." Devices, though, may or may not be read; they keep track of who is selecting on them and send notifications when they become ready. xnu provides structures and routines for tracking threads waiting for I/O and waking up those threads: see selrecord(), selthreadclear(), seltrue(), selwait(), selwakeup(), and the selinfo structure (sys/select.h).

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_exchange_args/1807210-vp.md): The vnode to check for I/O readiness.
- [which](vnop_exchange_args/1807214-which.md): What kind of I/O is desired: FREAD, FWRITE.
- [fflags](vnop_exchange_args/1807216-fflags.md): Flags from fileglob as seen in fcntl.h, e.g. O_NONBLOCK, O_APPEND.
- [wql](vnop_exchange_args/1807221-wql.md): Opaque object to pass to selrecord().
- [ctx](vnop_exchange_args/1807223-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for select request.

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_fsync_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Inform a filesystem that a file is no longer mapped.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_fsync_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

In general, no action is required of a filesystem for VNOP_MNOMAP.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_fsync_args/1807225-vp.md): The vnode which is no longer mapped.
- [ctx](vnop_fsync_args/1807227-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for mnomap request.

# Document: vnop_getattr_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_getattr_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_getattr_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_getattr_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to see if a kauth-style operation is permitted.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_getattr_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_ACCESS is currently only called on filesystems which mark themselves as doing their authentication remotely (vfs_setauthopaque(), vfs_authopaque()). A VNOP_ACCESS() calldown may come without any preceding VNOP_OPEN().

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_getattr_args/1807228-vp.md): File to authorize action for.
- [action](vnop_getattr_args/1807230-action.md): kauth-style action to be checked for permissions, e.g. KAUTH_VNODE_DELETE.
- [ctx](vnop_getattr_args/1807232-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate action.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_getattr_args/1586271-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_getattr_args/1586319-a_desc.md)
- [a_vap](vnop_getattr_args/1586168-a_vap.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_getattr_args/1585987-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_getxattr_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_getxattr_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_getxattr_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_getxattr_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Write data from a mapped file back to disk.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_getxattr_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_PAGEOUT() is called when data from a mapped file needs to be flushed to disk, either because of an msync() call or due to memory pressure. Filesystems are for the most part expected to just call cluster_pageout(). However, if they opt into the VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 flag, then they will be responsible for creating their own UPLs.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_getxattr_args/1807243-vp.md): The vnode for which to page out data.
- [pl](vnop_getxattr_args/1807247-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](vnop_getxattr_args/1807250-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](vnop_getxattr_args/1807253-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [size](vnop_getxattr_args/1807254-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [flags](vnop_getxattr_args/1807257-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](vnop_getxattr_args/1807260-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

### Instance Properties

# Document: vp

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_getxattr_args/1807243-vp
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_getxattr_args/1807243-vp
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vp

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The vnode for which to page out data.

## See Also

### Fields

- [pl](1807247-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](1807250-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](1807253-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [size](1807254-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [flags](1807257-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](1807260-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

- [size](1807254-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [ctx](1807260-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

# vnop_getxattr_desc

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Global Variable  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Write data from a mapped file back to disk.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnodeop_desc vnop_getxattr_desc;
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_PAGEOUT() is called when data from a mapped file needs to be flushed to disk, either because of an msync() call or due to memory pressure. Filesystems are for the most part expected to just call cluster_pageout(). However, if they opt into the VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 flag, then they will be responsible for creating their own UPLs.

The vnode for which to page out data.

UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.

Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.

Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.

Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.

UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.

Context to authenticate for pageout request.

# vnop_inactive_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to get the pathname represented by a symbolic link.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_inactive_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_READLINK() gets the path stored in a symbolic link; it is called by namei() and the readlink() system call.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_inactive_args/1807261-vp.md): Symbolic link to read from.
- [uio](vnop_inactive_args/1807265-uio.md): Destination information for link path.
- [ctx](vnop_inactive_args/1807268-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for readlink request.

# Document: vnop_link_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_link_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_link_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_link_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to delete a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_link_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_REMOVE is called to remove a file from a filesystem's namespace, for example by unlink(). It can operate on regular files, named pipes, special files, and in some cases on directories.

## Topics

### Fields

- [dvp](vnop_link_args/1807270-dvp.md): Directory in which to delete a file.
- [vp](vnop_link_args/1807271-vp.md): The file to delete.
- [cnp](vnop_link_args/1807272-cnp.md): Filename information.
- [ctx](vnop_link_args/1807273-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for fsync request.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The vnode from which to remove extended attributes.

Which attribute to delete.

XATTR_NOSECURITY: bypass security-checking.

Context to authenticate for attribute delete request.

# Document: vnop_mkdir_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_mkdir_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_mkdir_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_mkdir_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to rename a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_mkdir_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_RENAME() will only be called with a source and target on the same volume.

## Topics

### Fields

- [fdvp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807293-fdvp.md): Directory in which source file resides.
- [fvp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807295-fvp.md): File being renamed.
- [fcnp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807297-fcnp.md): Name information for source file.
- [tdvp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807300-tdvp.md): Directory file is being moved to.
- [tvp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807304-tvp.md): Existing file with same name as target, should one exist.
- [tcnp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807305-tcnp.md): Name information for target path.
- [ctx](vnop_mkdir_args/1807306-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for rename request.

# Document: vnop_mknod_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_mknod_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_mknod_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_mknod_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to create a whiteout.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_mknod_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Whiteouts are used to support the union filesystem, whereby one filesystem is mounted "transparently" on top of another. A whiteout in the upper layer of a union mount is a "deletion" of a file in the lower layer; lookups will catch the whiteout and fail, setting ISWHITEOUT in the componentname structure, even if an underlying file of the same name exists. The whiteout vnop is used for creation, deletion, and checking whether a directory supports whiteouts (see flags). also support the LOOKUP flag, which is used to test whether a directory supports whiteouts.

## Topics

### Fields

- [dvp](vnop_mknod_args/1807307-dvp.md): Directory in which to create.
- [cnp](vnop_mknod_args/1807310-cnp.md): Name information for whiteout.
- [flags](vnop_mknod_args/1807313-flags.md): CREATE: create a whiteout. LOOKUP: check whether a directory supports whiteouts, DELETE: remove a whiteout.
- [ctx](vnop_mknod_args/1807317-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate whiteout creation.

# Document: vnop_mmap_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_mmap_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_mmap_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_mmap_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to invalidate all open file descriptors for a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_mmap_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

This function is typically called as part of a TTY revoke, but can also be used on regular files. Most filesystems simply use nop_revoke(), which calls vn_revoke(), as their revoke vnop implementation.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_mmap_args/1807320-vp.md): The vnode to revoke.
- [flags](vnop_mmap_args/1807322-flags.md): Unused.
- [ctx](vnop_mmap_args/1807323-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for revoke request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_mmap_args/1585994-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_mmap_args/1586032-a_desc.md)
- [a_fflags](vnop_mmap_args/1586013-a_fflags.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_mmap_args/1585977-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_mnomap_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_mnomap_args

Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_mnomap_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Notify a filesystem that a file is being mmap-ed.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_mnomap_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_MMAP is an advisory calldown to say that the system is mmap-ing a file.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_mnomap_args/1807325-vp.md): The vnode being mmapped.
- [flags](vnop_mnomap_args/1807326-flags.md): Memory protection: PROT_READ, PROT_WRITE, PROT_EXEC.
- [ctx](vnop_mnomap_args/1807329-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for mmap request.

- [a_context](vnop_mnomap_args/1586101-a_context.md)

# Document: vnop_offtoblk_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_offtoblk_args

# vnop_offtoblk_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to convert a logical block number to a file offset.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_offtoblk_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_BLKTOOFF() converts a logical block to a file offset in bytes. That offset can be passed to VNOP_BLOCKMAP(), then, to get a physical block number--buf_strategy() does this.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_offtoblk_args/1807337-vp.md): The vnode for which to convert a logical block to an offset.
- [lblkno](vnop_offtoblk_args/1807345-lblkno.md): Logical block number to turn into offset.
- [offset](vnop_offtoblk_args/1807353-offset.md): Destination for file offset.

### Instance Properties

- [a_desc](vnop_offtoblk_args/1585993-a_desc.md)
- [a_lblkno](vnop_offtoblk_args/1586293-a_lblkno.md)
- [a_offset](vnop_offtoblk_args/1586020-a_offset.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_offtoblk_args/1586202-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_open_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_open_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_open_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_open_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to create a special file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_open_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The mknod vnop is used to create character and block device files, named pipe (FIFO) files, and named sockets. The newly created file should be returned with an iocount which will be dropped by the caller. A VNOP_MKNOD() call can come down without a preceding VNOP_OPEN().

## Topics

### Fields

- [dvp](vnop_open_args/1807362-dvp.md): Directory in which to create the special file.
- [vpp](vnop_open_args/1807367-vpp.md): Destination for newly created vnode.
- [cnp](vnop_open_args/1807373-cnp.md): Name information for new file.
- [vap](vnop_open_args/1807377-vap.md): Attributes for new file, including type.
- [ctx](vnop_open_args/1807385-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate node creation.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_open_args/1586175-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_open_args/1586128-a_desc.md)
- [a_mode](vnop_open_args/1586035-a_mode.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_open_args/1586115-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_pagein_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_pagein_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_pagein_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_pagein_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Pre-allocate space for a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_pagein_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_ALLOCATE() changes the amount of backing store set aside to a file. It can be used to either shrink or grow a file. If the file shrinks, its ubc size will be modified accordingly, but if it grows, then the ubc size is unchanged; space is set aside without being actively used by the file. VNOP_ALLOCATE() is currently only called as part of the F_PREALLOCATE fcntl.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_pagein_args/1807403-vp.md): The vnode for which to preallocate space.
- [length](vnop_pagein_args/1807414-length.md): Desired preallocated file length.
- [flags](vnop_pagein_args/1807426-flags.md): PREALLOCATE: preallocate allocation blocks. ALLOCATECONTIG: allocate contigious space. ALLOCATEALL: allocate all requested space or no space at all. FREEREMAINDER: deallocate allocated but unfilled blocks. ALLOCATEFROMPEOF: allocate from the physical eof. ALLOCATEFROMVOL: allocate from the volume offset.
- [bytesallocated](vnop_pagein_args/1807437-bytesallocated.md): Additional bytes set aside for file. Set to 0 if none are allocated OR if the file is contracted.
- [offset](vnop_pagein_args/1807450-offset.md): Hint for where to find free blocks.
- [ctx](vnop_pagein_args/1807464-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for allocation request.

# vp

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The vnode for which to preallocate space.

## See Also

### Fields

- [length](1807414-length.md): Desired preallocated file length.
- [flags](1807426-flags.md): PREALLOCATE: preallocate allocation blocks. ALLOCATECONTIG: allocate contigious space. ALLOCATEALL: allocate all requested space or no space at all. FREEREMAINDER: deallocate allocated but unfilled blocks. ALLOCATEFROMPEOF: allocate from the physical eof. ALLOCATEFROMVOL: allocate from the volume offset.
- [bytesallocated](1807437-bytesallocated.md): Additional bytes set aside for file. Set to 0 if none are allocated OR if the file is contracted.
- [offset](1807450-offset.md): Hint for where to find free blocks.
- [ctx](1807464-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for allocation request.

# Document: vnop_pageout_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_pageout_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_pageout_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_pageout_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Pull file data into memory.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_pageout_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_PAGEIN() is called by when a process faults on data mapped from a file or when madvise() demands pre-fetching. It is conceptually somewhat similar to VNOP_READ(). Filesystems are typically expected to call cluster_pagein() to handle the labor of mapping and committing the UPL.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_pageout_args/1807482-vp.md): The vnode for which to page in data.
- [pl](vnop_pageout_args/1807490-pl.md): UPL describing pages needing to be paged in.
- [pl_offset](vnop_pageout_args/1807495-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL at which to start placing data.
- [f_offset](vnop_pageout_args/1807502-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged in.
- [size](vnop_pageout_args/1807509-size.md): Amount of data to page in (in bytes).
- [flags](vnop_pageout_args/1807514-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](vnop_pageout_args/1807517-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pagein request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_pageout_args/1586273-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_pageout_args/1586315-a_desc.md)

# Document: vnop_pathconf_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_pathconf_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_pathconf_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_pathconf_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Release filesystem-internal resources for a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_pathconf_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_RECLAIM() is called as part of the process of recycling a vnode. During a reclaim routine, a filesystem should remove a vnode from its hash and deallocate any resources allocated to that vnode. VFS guarantees that when VNOP_RECLAIM() is called, there are no more iocount references on a vnode (though there may still be usecount references--these are invalidated by the reclaim) and that no more will be granted. This means in practice that there will be no filesystem calls on the vnode being reclaimed until the reclaim has finished and the vnode has been reused.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_pathconf_args/1807521-vp.md): The vnode to reclaim.
- [ctx](vnop_pathconf_args/1807524-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for reclaim.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_pathconf_args/1586224-a_context.md)

# Document: vnop_read_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_read_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_read_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_read_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to set vnode attributes.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_read_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Supported attributes ("Yes, I am setting this attribute.") are set with VATTR_SET_SUPPORTED. Requested attributes are checked with VATTR_IS_ACTIVE. Attribute values are accessed directly through structure fields. VNOP_SETATTR() is the core of the KPI function vnode_setattr(), which is used by chmod(), chown(), truncate(), and many others. A VNOP_SETATTR() call may come without any preceding VNOP_OPEN().

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_read_args/1807536-vp.md): The vnode whose attributes to set.
- [vap](vnop_read_args/1807548-vap.md): Container for which attributes are to be set and their desired values, as well as for the filesystem to return information about which attributes were successfully set.
- [ctx](vnop_read_args/1807562-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate request for attribute change.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_read_args/1586075-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_read_args/1586154-a_desc.md)
- [a_ioflag](vnop_read_args/1586062-a_ioflag.md)
- [a_uio](vnop_read_args/1586244-a_uio.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_read_args/1586097-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_readdir_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_readdir_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_readdir_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_readdir_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to create a symbolic link.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_readdir_args {
    ...
};
```

## Topics

### Fields

- [If](vnop_readdir_args/1807590-if.md): VNOP_SYMLINK() is successful, the new file should be returned with an iocount which will be dropped by the caller. VFS does not ensure that the target path will have a length shorter than the max symlink length for the filesystem.
- [dvp](vnop_readdir_args/1807603-dvp.md): Parent directory for new symlink file.
- [vpp](vnop_readdir_args/1807609-vpp.md)
- [cnp](vnop_readdir_args/1807615-cnp.md): Name information for new symlink.
- [vap](vnop_readdir_args/1807617-vap.md): Attributes for symlink.
- [target](vnop_readdir_args/1807620-target.md): Path for symlink to store; for "ln -s /var/vardir linktovardir", "target" would be "/var/vardir"
- [ctx](vnop_readdir_args/1807622-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for symlink request.

# If

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

VNOP_SYMLINK() is successful, the new file should be returned with an iocount which will be dropped by the caller. VFS does not ensure that the target path will have a length shorter than the max symlink length for the filesystem.

# Document: vnop_readdirattr_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_readdirattr_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_readdirattr_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_readdirattr_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to enumerate directory entries.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_readdirattr_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_READDIR() packs a buffer with "struct dirent" directory entry representations as described by the "getdirentries" manual page.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807627-vp.md): Directory to enumerate.
- [uio](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807633-uio.md): Destination information for resulting direntries.
- [flags](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807637-flags.md): VNODE_READDIR_EXTENDED, VNODE_READDIR_REQSEEKOFF, VNODE_READDIR_SEEKOFF32: Apple-internal flags.
- [eofflag](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807642-eofflag.md): Should be set to 1 if the end of the directory has been reached.
- [numdirent](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807646-numdirent.md): Should be set to number of entries written into buffer.
- [ctx](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807650-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for readdir request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_actualcount](vnop_readdirattr_args/1586012-a_actualcount.md)

# Document: vnop_readlink_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_readlink_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_readlink_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_readlink_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to get file attributes for many files in a directory at once.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_readlink_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_READDIRATTR() packs a buffer with file attributes, as if the results of many "getattrlist" calls.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_readlink_args/1807660-vp.md): Directory in which to enumerate entries' attributes.
- [alist](vnop_readlink_args/1807668-alist.md): Which attributes are wanted for each directory entry.
- [uio](vnop_readlink_args/1807675-uio.md): Destination information for resulting attributes.
- [maxcount](vnop_readlink_args/1807683-maxcount.md): Maximum count of files to get attributes for.
- [options](vnop_readlink_args/1807690-options.md): FSOPT_NOFOLLOW: do not follow symbolic links. FSOPT_NOINMEMUPDATE: do not use data which have been updated since an inode was loaded into memory.
- [newstate](vnop_readlink_args/1807697-newstate.md): The "newstate" should be set to a value which changes if the contents of a directory change through an addition or deletion but stays the same otherwise.
- [eofflag](vnop_readlink_args/1807701-eofflag.md): Should be set to 1 if the end of the directory has been reached.
- [actualcount](vnop_readlink_args/1807705-actualcount.md): Should be set to number of files whose attributes were written into buffer.
- [ctx](vnop_readlink_args/1807709-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for readdirattr request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_readlink_args/1586279-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_readlink_args/1585957-a_desc.md)
- [a_uio](vnop_readlink_args/1586135-a_uio.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_readlink_args/1586334-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_reclaim_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_reclaim_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_reclaim_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_reclaim_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Notify a filesystem that the last usecount (persistent reference) on a vnode has been dropped.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_reclaim_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_INACTVE() gives a filesystem a chance to aggressively release resources assocated with a vnode, perhaps even to call vnode_recycle(), but no action is prescribed; it is acceptable for VNOP_INACTIVE to be a no-op and to defer all reclamation until VNOP_RECLAIM(). VNOP_INACTVE() will not be called on a vnode if no persistent reference is ever taken; an important example is a stat(), which takes an iocount, reads its data, and drops that iocount.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_reclaim_args/1807717-vp.md): The vnode which is now inactive.
- [ctx](vnop_reclaim_args/1807721-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for inactive message.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_reclaim_args/1586259-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_reclaim_args/1586039-a_desc.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_reclaim_args/1586146-a_vp.md)

# vnop_rename_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to create a hardlink to a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_rename_args {
    ...
};
```

## Discussion

See "man 2 link".

- [cnp](vnop_rename_args/1807759-cnp.md): Filename information for new link.
- [ctx](vnop_rename_args/1807761-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for link request.

# Document: vnop_revoke_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_revoke_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_revoke_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_revoke_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to atomically exchange the data of two files.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_revoke_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_EXCHANGE() is currently only called by the exchangedata() system call. It will only be applied to files on the same volume.

## Topics

### Fields

- [fvp](vnop_revoke_args/1807765-fvp.md): First vnode.
- [tvp](vnop_revoke_args/1807769-tvp.md): Second vnode.
- [options](vnop_revoke_args/1807772-options.md): Unused.
- [ctx](vnop_revoke_args/1807776-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for exchangedata request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_revoke_args/1586055-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_revoke_args/1585984-a_desc.md)
- [a_flags](vnop_revoke_args/1586113-a_flags.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_revoke_args/1586122-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_rmdir_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_rmdir_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_rmdir_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_rmdir_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to create a directory.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_rmdir_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The newly created directory should be returned with an iocount which will be dropped by the caller.

## Topics

### Fields

- [dvp](vnop_rmdir_args/1807781-dvp.md): Directory in which to create new directory.
- [vpp](vnop_rmdir_args/1807786-vpp.md): Destination for pointer to new directory's vnode.
- [cnp](vnop_rmdir_args/1807788-cnp.md): Name information for new directory.
- [vap](vnop_rmdir_args/1807790-vap.md): Attributes for new directory.
- [ctx](vnop_rmdir_args/1807793-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for mkdir request.

### Instance Properties

# Document: vnop_searchfs_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_searchfs_args
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_searchfs_args
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vnop_searchfs_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Write data from a mapped file back to disk.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_searchfs_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_PAGEOUT() is called when data from a mapped file needs to be flushed to disk, either because of an msync() call or due to memory pressure. Filesystems are for the most part expected to just call cluster_pageout(). However, if they opt into the VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 flag, then they will be responsible for creating their own UPLs.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_searchfs_args/1807795-vp.md): The vnode for which to page out data.
- [pl](vnop_searchfs_args/1807798-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](vnop_searchfs_args/1807800-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](vnop_searchfs_args/1807802-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [size](vnop_searchfs_args/1807803-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [flags](vnop_searchfs_args/1807804-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](vnop_searchfs_args/1807805-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

# Document: vp

Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_searchfs_args/1807795-vp
Description: Interface language: Objective-C

# vp

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The vnode for which to page out data.

## See Also

### Fields

- [pl](1807798-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](1807800-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](1807802-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [size](1807803-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [flags](1807804-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](1807805-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.
